key_insight: A dynamic Mixture of Feature Difference module improves synthesis of contrast-enhanced MRI from non-contrast brain MRI by learning both sequence-specific features and their explicit differences.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce the need for contrast-agent injections, lowering scan risk and cost while helping support tumor visualization and downstream segmentation.
method: Uses multiple non-contrast MRI sequences as input for CE-MRI synthesis.
Adaptively weights informative source features and inter-sequence differences via MoFD.
Includes an adversarial or regression-based training variant to balance perceptual quality and structural fidelity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports superior fidelity and perceptual quality on UCSF-PDGM and UPenn-GBM, with reconstructed tumor regions and segmentation performance comparable to real CE-MRI.
watch_item: Performance is dataset-dependent and the adversarial variant may improve visual realism at the expense of structural fidelity, so external validation is important.
paper_title: Mixture of Multi-Sequence Feature Difference for Contrast-Enhanced MRI Synthesis
